updatedBy: The release commit that cuts the version, alongside the npm dist-tag pin. `stable` is the version `go get ...@latest` resolves, and `prerelease` is the newest `go/v<version>-next.<n>` tag if one is ahead of it. The Go module proxy has no dist-tags and no unpublish, so this file is the only record of what the second implementation actually serves. `npm run check:release-parity` reads it against the npm pin and the two version strings in the tree. See RELEASING.md.

knownGap.reason: go/v0.19.0 was pushed as a bare tag on 2026-09-02, before RELEASING.md set the prerelease rule, and it is the only version the proxy has. A Go tag cannot be unpublished, so the gap closes when 0.19.0 is promoted on npm or when the next release publishes both together. Remove this field and the --allow-known-gap flag at that point.
